claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic CoCrFeNi.
Baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits low friction at room temperature.
Baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits increased friction at elevated temperatures.
Baseline CoCrFeNi exhibits increased wear at elevated temperatures.
The elevated-temperature degradation of baseline CoCrFeNi is caused by uncontrolled oxide formation and tribochemical reactions.
The intervention is to add approximately 1 at% Ti to CoCrFeNi.
A minor Ti addition will enable formation of a stable, low-shear oxide tribofilm throughout sliding from room temperature to 800 °C.
Ti will promote preferential formation of a finely dispersed and adherent oxide phase.
The Ti-containing oxide may be a mixed spinel or rutile/TiO2 phase.
The Ti-containing oxide will act as a lubricious tribofilm at high temperatures.
Approximately 1 at% Ti will preserve the alloy's favorable solid-solution microstructure at low temperatures.
At elevated temperatures, Ti oxidizes more readily than the parent Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni constituents.
Preferential Ti oxidation will produce a continuous protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer will reduce friction and wear by providing a low-shear interface.
At low temperatures, the small Ti addition will not significantly disrupt the solid-solution properties and will therefore maintain low friction.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, Ti-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction throughout the 25–800 °C range.
Relative to unmodified CoCrFeNi, Ti-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate throughout the 25–800 °C range.
The largest tribological improvement is expected near 800 °C.
The claimed performance applies to dry sliding in ambient air from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under matched load and sliding-speed conditions.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis attributes low friction over the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range to a stable oxide tribofilm, whereas the detailed mechanism invokes oxide-film lubrication only at elevated temperature and attributes low-temperature behavior to preservation of the underlying solid solution.
